decisions.reason: Its continued home-page prominence across 2023 and 2024 suggests strong strategic fit and enough traction that the option value of keeping it open remains high relative to likely carrying costs.

Although software for oncology risk management appears somewhat less central to a hardware-oriented manufacturer and may require ongoing support, it has remained on a dedicated page for two years so uncertainty is not yet resolved enough to justify abandonment.
As a 2024 launch in a closely related medical imaging QA niche, it is still in the early option stage and is inexpensive enough to keep available while market feedback accumulates.
This 2024 mammography phantom fits the firm's apparent imaging-quality portfolio, and with only one year of evidence the firm would typically preserve the option unless clear failure had appeared.

It is new, adjacent to the firm's core capabilities, and despite some possible overlap with other mammography phantoms the cost of keeping it listed is likely low compared with the value of learning demand.

Medical imaging quality assurance instruments look highly consistent with the firm's broader product logic, so the firm would likely continue the product while uncertainty about adoption and follow-on sales resolves.
